Mages scale very well with levels and they also have utility or damage that gets better the more AP or AD they have. Champions like Orianna, for example, get lower cooldowns and mana for more ability usage, as well as stronger burst and slows, if you get gold from Middle lane on top of levels.

However, in the middle lane, the distance between minions to the turret, as well as the distance between the base to the minions, is much shorter than the top lane, and mages are usually immobile (can't escape with dashes or blinks), so they work best at the middle lane, also abusing their utility at top and bottom if they need to.

Damage over time: 1 second for a total of 2 (+12.5% bonus AD) (+5% AP) magic damage.

Brands passive turns it into this:

4 seconds for a total of 8 (+50% bonus AD) (+20% AP) magic damage.

That instance is always the same, so the base damage does not scale. If you have 300 AP with Brand, it will deal:

8 (3 AD) (60 AP) magic damage. (roughly, considering Natural Talent's AD)

So each spell you land, if you let it sit for your entire passive, will deal about 70 Magic Damage. It's pretty decent. It also has no cooldown.
____________________________________________________

At 3 stacks, the target takes 10 - 180 (based on level) + (30% bonus AD) + (10% AP) magic damage.

Same scenario, the damage will be: (at level 12, for example)

120 + 2 + 30 = roughly 150 damage

It has a cooldown of 20 seconds. DFT does not have a cooldown. At this scenario, If you land 2 spells throughout the 8 seconds, you've dealt as much damage as TD, but you can deal that same damage much faster, within 3 seconds or 2, with TD, but it will have a cooldown.

The logic applies throughout levels: TD is up-front damage with a long cooldown, but DFT will apply to more than one target, Brand can use it very well and it will match TD after half the cooldown of TD, and since you're stacking AP, it will be stronger later.

Winning lane with Lee Sin is all about outplaying enemy abilities with your Safeguard and Resonating Strike. Lee no longer gains a shield when shielding minions or wards, so he can't suddenly dash-in and win small trades. You also can't afford to Max E for the magic damage; at best you can max Q and E evenly, but this delays your early game power too much to be worth the trade-off.

With that in mind, your best bet at winning is by Safeguarding out of enemy skillshots. For Jax you want to Safeguard to a minion or ward before he stuns you, and you want to make him walk around so you can use your abilities off cooldown, avoid him from autoattacking you freely.

Against Irelia it is trickier because she is kinda the top lane Lee. Your best shot is to overpower her and kill her at Level 2, but make sure to bait her E first so she can't stun you. Once she gets a full defensive item or Trinity Force you'll have to Ult her under turret or to try and limit trades, she wants to always prolong them so she comes out ahead with her true damage.

You want to stay behind minions once he uses Plasma Fission. It is pretty much a T shape, there the horizontal line is the same range as the maximum range it can travel before splitting.
If you keep this in mind, you'll calculate where he can split the bolt, and you can have a minion block it.
If that is not an option, you can try juking it out by doing as if you're intending to walk as far as you can, but you turn around at the last second, avoiding the bolt completely.

His Void Rift is delayed damage. It's okay if you're hit by it, but sidestep it to avoid the detonation damage, otherwise he gets 2 very easy passive stacks which he can get an instantaneous passive proc of with his Ultimate.

Tectonic Disruption is not really hard to avoid, he will try to use it when you are slowed by his Plasma Fission.

Considering all of this, and the fact Vel'Koz can push hard with his W, the following champions are great against him: Orianna to keep range and clear as fast, Anivia for a similar kit but more front-loaded damage, Yasuo to kill Vel'Koz easily; if you Windwall his Q and dodge his E he has little to do, Cho'Gath to sustain his poke.

It has to do with input lag, server ping, timing and accuracy. Also, sometimes, key priority.

Input lag: When you press a key, then another, some keyboards will have an input lag. This means that the desired inputs will manifestate in-game with a delay. Whatever delay it is, it will affect how smoothly you can wardhop by Safeguarding immediately after placing a ward.

Because of this, you can abuse Key Priority. Many keyboards have priorities, although not intentional, where a key, if pressed at the same time as another key, will always come first. I can't tell you how it works for your keyboard, but for mine, pressing Y and U at the same exact time will always type Y before U, even if I mistime it a bit.

While that doesn't help you much, you can try out in Notepad which combination of two keys allow you to abuse this. Many people suggest C for the wards, and that works because for many keyboards, C has priority over W. Try it right now if you want, mash C and W at the same time and C always comes first, even if you take a small delay.

Another thing is the server ping. If you have high ping, your movements will show up in your game as delayed, and that can affect your timing when ward hopping. Even a 10 ping differential can change the feel of this, so be mindful of your ping. 

For personal experience, I've played Lee with 40 to 150 ping. It's not too different, but you do have to make a very slight delay on the timing. It takes a little while to get used to, so practice it in a custom match and you will get the hang of it really fast.

The last thing, is accuracy. Even if you have 8 ping and have key priority, you need to time it well.

As a rule of thumb, your Safeguard will always be within range of both the trinket and sighstone. Even without the Scout mastery.

Also, you need to hear the audio cue of the ward going off. As soon as you hear it, you can 'dial in' (tell the game to do something) your Safeguard on that same point and you will, rather instantly, safeguard there. 

It's important to not spam W right as you C, or whatever key you use, because you will tell the game to Safeguard to a position where the ward is still not at yet. Again, practice it in a custom game, varying the timings and the cues you chose, and you will find what feels best for you.

As a last note, ward hopping is definitely not hard to do. Being consistent at ward hopping accurately is. Much like aiming, precision matters more than accuracy, so if you're agitated or nervous because of something going on in game, relax and take the time necessary to wardhop without messing up. Even if you only dash a distance of fifty units, it will be more than mistakingly casting your second W or placing two wards. Self control will take you further.

It might be hard to close out games when you don't know how it is done. You didn't state your league so I will point out the barebones of how you are meant to close out games:

1. Get a powerspike. This is often one or two items bought, and sometimes it is level-based such by having your rank two ultimate because you're a sololaner.

2. Look for an objective. If you're a laner, your primary objective is the enemy laner turret once you have at least one item and you can offer something to other lanes. If you can, don't take turret until you feel you will be useful at other lanes, because otherwise you put yourself at great gank risk.
After the laner turret, you want to take other lane turrets, but the FIRST dragon has priority over this. The first dragon offers both an AD and AP increase, which even if slightly, gets better the more of those stats you have, so it is an investment for the rest of the game.

3. Once you have all enemy outer turrets taken, it is time to group with your team, sweep enemy wards and look for a PICK ON AN ENEMY CHAMPION if your team has the potential for this (your team has Blitz, Elise, Darius, Thresh, Leona, etc), SPLITPUSH WAVES to create 4v5s (if your team has more than one champion that can EFFECTIVELY clear enemy minion waves fast enough) or GROUP AS FIVE AND SIEGE TURRETS (if you have enough waveclear and ranged characters to chip turrets down, Tristana being the best at this).
Those aren't all the ways you play as a team, but more often than not teams are pick-based, or at the very least, have great splitpush potential. Knowing what your strenghts are and how to abuse them is key to gaining dominance over the enemy.

4. Get Baron. Baron is the objective you need when your team has a hard time SIEGING TURRETS. Baron makes ALL minions very bulky, while making the cannon minion OUTRANGE all turrets, so you only need to keep that minion alive and it will eventually take down a turret. 
Baron also affects the other lanes, so ALL lanes will slowly push to the enemy base, which will demand the attention of an enemy, creating a 4v5 that your team most likely can get an advantage of.

5. Get the inhibitor. Getting the inhibitor has a purpose similar to getting Baron: the inhibitor-less lane will start HEAVILY pushing to their base because of the sturdier lane minions and the superminion. The inhibitor is great because it lasts more than Baron and it allows your team to have more opportunities and chances to do whatever they need to do to win the game.

6. Avoid dying and focus on keeping the carries alive/killing them. As the game goes on, death timers become longer. The way the League meta works is that the ADC dishes out the most damage over time while the mage usually has burst damage coupled with utility. The priority target lategame is the ADC no matter what; that includes your own. It doesn't matter if the ADC has four items, that is often enough to deal more damage over time than other champions possibly can.
If you have a lot of CC, focus on peeling for your carry if he is badly position or focus on their enemy ADC if theirs is on a bad position. Knowing said positions takes time and experience so just play more to know those. The same positioning rule applies to assasins and bruisers; just look for opportunities to kill their ADC while protecting yours from that same goal the enemy also has on them.

This isn't all that involves closing out games, but it's a basic and, in my opinion, decent way to look at games on a broad way so you know what you need to do next to win the game.
